responsibility: Provides rustc’s shared source-location and naming infrastructure: the crate root (`lib.rs`) defines the core span, position, source-file, session-global, serialization, and stable-hashing framework that the rest of the compiler uses to attach locations and identities to syntax and definitions. Its source-text layer combines `analyze_source_file`, which scans UTF-8 input into line-start and multibyte-character metadata, with `source_map`, which manages loaded source files, path remapping, and translation between byte positions, lines, columns, snippets, and macro-origin locations; `caching_source_map_view` adds a memoizing view for repeated line/column lookups used by diagnostics and hashing, and `tests.rs` covers crate-wide span/source-file behaviors such as line lookup, newline normalization, and trimming. For compact and provenance-rich spans, `span_encoding` implements the efficient in-memory encoding of spans, while `hygiene` tracks macro-expansion contexts, expansion IDs, transparency, and cross-crate hygiene state so spans preserve macro provenance and name-resolution behavior. The crate also provides compiler-wide identity and language-context support through `def_id`, which defines crate and definition identity types plus stable hashes and encoding for cross-session/cross-crate item identification, and `edition`, which defines Rust edition values and helpers used by parsing and keyword logic. Its naming subsystem is centered on `symbol`, which implements interned symbols, keywords, identifier helpers, and edition-aware keyword classification, and is complemented by `lev_distance`, which supplies Unicode-aware edit-distance and best-match selection utilities for diagnostics and name suggestions. Finally, `fatal_error` defines the special unrecoverable-error marker and unwinding path used to abort compilation cleanly, and `profiling` adds self-profiling helpers that record span-bearing events. Together, these modules make `rustc_span` the compiler crate responsible for representing, encoding, interning, mapping, and profiling source spans, identifiers, editions, macro hygiene, and stable definition identities across the compiler.
